note: U11 opening (spec §4). Scenes with the same id in a campaign list replace the shared one. Text is a placeholder draft for the owner to review; every effect is data (spec §20). Variables: {player} {friend} {parent} {coach} {position} {club}.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Okay. Serious question. You know I'm at {club} now, right?

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Thursday training. Coach said I could bring someone. I said I know exactly one person who can actually receive a pass.
{friend} is trying very hard to look casual about it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: So? Thursday. You'd just come and train. Nobody signs anything.

choices.label: "What's it actually like? Like — proper coaching?"

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Proper. Coach Code yells, but he yells useful things. You'll see. Thursday, four-thirty.

choices.label: "I don't know. Rec is fine. Everyone there is better than me."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Half of them can't do what you just did with that first touch. Come once. If you hate it, I'll never mention it again. Probably.

choices.label: "Finally. I've wanted to play for a real club for a year."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: A year? You could've said something! Okay. Thursday. Bring shin pads, Coach checks.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: That's what I told Coach you'd say. Thursday. Don't be late, he does this thing with his whistle.

lines.text: The fields sit behind a middle school, three of them in a row, sprinklers still ticking off on the far one. The light is the colour of orange soda.
{friend} is waiting at the edge of the parking lot, ball under one arm, already in the training top.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You came. Okay. Okay okay okay. Rules: when he blows the whistle, you stop and look at him. That's it. That's the whole secret.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Also I told him you play {position}. Was that right? Too late, it's right now.
A whistle, sharp enough to make the far field flinch. A man with a clipboard he never looks at walks over, sun behind him.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're {player}. {friend} has been telling me about you for two weeks, which is two weeks longer than I've heard about anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Rec soccer, couple of years, plays {position}. Good. Here's what I care about tonight: not how fast you are, not whether you score. Whether you look before the ball arrives.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Shin pads? Show me. — Good. Water over there. Go stand with the ball-hog.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: He means me. It's a compliment. It's mostly a compliment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Simple. I play you the ball. Someone comes to take it. Three gates. Your first touch takes the ball through the gate that's AWAY from the pressure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Look before it gets to you. Where's the defender coming from? Then touch. One touch, through a gate. Go.
The other group finishes. Coach Code waves everyone in with the clipboard.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You looked. Every time, you checked where the pressure was before the ball got there. That's the thing I can't teach in a week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Sometimes you looked, sometimes you guessed. The guesses are the ones that got taken off you. Look first. Always.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You rushed it. Ball's coming and your head is down. Not a crime, everyone does it here at first. But it's the whole game.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: And the touch was clean. Weight of it, direction. Rec did something right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Touch was heavy. You'll fix that with a wall and a hundred boring evenings. I'll give you the boring evenings.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: {friend}. Stop grinning. You're not the one who did it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Told you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Go home. Talk to your family. If you want to come back, Tuesday, same time. If you don't, that's fine too, you'll be a better rec player than you were an hour ago.
Sunday afternoon. The ball has been sitting by the door since Thursday like it's waiting for an answer too.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: So. Tuesday's the day. What are we doing?

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Then we do it properly. Bag packed Monday night. And you tell {friend} yourself, not me.

choices.label: "Can we try it for a month first?"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: A month. That's a grown-up answer. A month, and then we talk honestly — both of us.

lines.text: The park behind the strip mall has one goal with no net and a patch of grass the sprinklers actually reach. It has been yours and {friend}'s since second grade.
{friend} pings the ball at you from way too far, the way he always does, and yells 'ONE TOUCH' before it has even landed.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: See, that! That thing you do where it just sticks to your foot. Nobody on my team can do that. Owen definitely can't, and he's the keeper.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Dev tried it last week and the ball ended up in the parking lot.
Dad picks you up late, still in his work shirt, radio on the traffic station he never listens to.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Mateo's mom texted me. Something about Thursday?
He is doing the thing where he watches the road very carefully.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Club soccer is a lot, bud. It's three nights a week, it's weekends, and it's not free. I'm not saying no. I'm saying I want to know what you're asking for.

choices.label: "It's just one training. I want to see what it's like."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: One training I can do. I'll move my shift. But we talk after — properly, not 'it was fine'.

choices.label: "School comes first. I promise. I'll show you."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's a promise, not a sentence. I'm going to remember it. Thursday, then.

choices.label: "Mateo's mom said she can drive. You wouldn't have to do anything."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: 'Wouldn't have to do anything.' Right. Okay. Go Thursday. Tell Mateo's mom thank you.

lines.text: Grass stains, a bruise you don't remember getting, and a plate of something Dad reheated twice.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Well?

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I watched a bit from the fence. The loud one — that's the coach? He seemed to like you.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Mateo's mom said you looked like you belonged there. Her words.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Mateo's mom said the coach spent more time on you than anyone. She meant it nicely. I think.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Homework first, then you tell me. Deal's a deal.
Your phone buzzes. Mateo: 'well??????' Seven question marks.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Okay. Then here's the deal: I'll figure out the money. You figure out the eight o'clock alarm.
You text back one word. Mateo replies with a photo of himself already asleep in his training top.

choices.label: "Can I think about it over the weekend?"

repair.label: Text Mateo that you need the weekend

response.speaker: parent
response.text: You can. That's a good answer, actually. Sunday we decide, together.

lines.text: The cul-de-sac ends in a wall that has taken ten thousand passes. Someone painted a goal on it years ago; you and {friend} have been arguing about whether the crossbar counts since kindergarten.
{friend} has her notebook open on the kerb — actual diagrams — and is trying to get you to run a pattern she saw on TV.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: No, you go and THEN I play it. If I play it first you're just standing there like a lamp.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: ...okay, that one was good. That was really good. Zoe can't do that and she scores every week.
Mom is on her laptop at the kitchen table, the one with the wobbly leg, doing two things at once and listening anyway.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Nia's club. Thursday. I heard about it from Nia's dad before I heard about it from you, which — noted.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I looked at their site. It's a lot of driving, and it's not cheap, and your brother has band on Thursdays. I'm not saying no. Tell me why.

choices.label: "It's one training. I just want to see it."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: One training. I'll swap with your brother's carpool. And you'll tell me what you actually thought — not 'it was fine'.

choices.label: "School stays first. I promise. Check my planner whenever you want."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: I will check the planner. That's not a threat, it's a promise back. Thursday.

choices.label: "Nia's dad can drive. You don't have to change anything."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Fine. Go Thursday. Say thank you to Nia's dad. Loudly.

lines.text: Your brother is practising the same four bars of trombone through the wall. Mom closes the laptop, which she never does.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: So?

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I stayed by the car. The coach shouts a lot. But he shouted your name like he'd already decided something.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Nia's dad said you were the only one who looked up before the ball came. He notices things like that.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Nia's dad said the coach kept saying your name. He didn't say what about. He notices things like that.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Planner first. Then soccer. I'm listening while you get it.
Your phone lights up on the counter. Nia: a photo of her notebook. A new page. It has your name on it.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Then we're doing it. I'll work out the driving with Nia's dad. You work out how to fall asleep before ten.
You text Nia one word. She sends back a diagram with two stick figures and an arrow. The arrow is you.

choices.label: "Can I think about it over the weekend?"

repair.label: Text Nia that you need the weekend

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Yes. And I'd rather you took the weekend than said yes to make Nia happy. Sunday, we decide.
